subject: zot
title: Zotfiles: downloadable portable agents with enforced permission manifests and consent receipts
one_why: Packages an agent (prompt+tools+permissions) as a local dir, .zot archive, or temporary GitHub download; load refuses unenforcible permission declarations, bundled executables, and tar traversal, and consent writes durable receipts -- no anchor ships a distribution format for agents with enforceably-checked scopes.

subject: zot
title: Skills exposed as name+description+source-pointer in system prompt, full body via skill tool
one_why: Compact registry line includes a trust pointer (builtin vs user SKILL.md path) so the model can reason about provenance before loading -- a small honesty wrinkle on the converging lazy-skill pattern.

subject: zot
title: Explicit 4-breakpoint cache budget with independently-cacheable OAuth identity prefix
one_why: Breakpoints allocated identity/system/last-tool/last-message so midnight-date drift in the user prompt cannot invalidate the identity prefix; Bedrock cachePoint gated on catalog cache-write price as capability proxy -- cache discipline most Go subjects lack.

subject: zot
title: Yolo is the default: approval gate exists only behind --no-yolo and jail only behind opt-in
one_why: Tools run unasked unless the user knows to pass --no-yolo, and the path jail starts unlocked; the tested, well-ordered guard-before-approval pipeline (cli.go:817-830) protects nobody on the default path -- same wrong-default shape as nanocoder.

subject: zot
title: Jailed bash policy is a substring deny-list the code itself admits cannot sandbox a shell
one_why: Banned patterns like 'rm -rf /' and 'sudo ' catch accidents, not adversaries (interpreters, quoting, aliases bypass); honestly documented, but it is the gating layer whenever jail is on -- no OS-level sandbox anywhere in packages/.

subject: zot
title: Auto-compact keyed on last-turn measured input tokens plus a pre-send condense pass
one_why: Trigger uses provider-reported input tokens vs context window rather than char estimates, and re-fires the queued prompt after compacting pre-turn -- reactive (last turn, not projected next), so one oversized prompt can still overflow before the guard acts.

subject: zot
title: Swarm crash-recovery via immutable meta.json + events.jsonl with StatusDetached reload
one_why: Immutable-identity meta files avoid concurrent-writer stomping; after a crash every subagent re-registers detached from disk and is viewable/resumable in the dashboard -- clean minimal journal vs crush's absent swarm persistence.
